Each business's current rating is on the Food Standards Agency website.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Students at Hopwood Hall College will receive weekly training from Rochdale AFC coaches through a new partnership starting in September 2027. The college’s BTEC Sport with Football qualification will be delivered with the club at its Middleton Campus. Students enrolling on the course will have the opportunity to attend one free match each term at Crown Oil Arena and play a fixture at the stadium at the end of each season. The partnership covers the college’s boys’ and girls’ football teams. Rochdale AFC’s scholars have also begun taking lessons at Hopwood Hall’s Middleton Campus, where facilities include a floodlit 3G pitch and four grass pitches. Julia Heap OBE, principal and chief executive of Hopwood Hall College, said: “We’re delighted to be working alongside Rochdale AFC and are very excited about what this partnership means for young people who are pursuing their passion for football. “The club shares our ambition for nurturing local talent and ensuring they’re able to perform at the top of their game right here in Rochdale.” Laura Thomas, chief executive of Rochdale AFC, said: “This is an exciting partnership for Rochdale AFC and one that allows us to continue making a positive impact in our local community.

candidates.source_title: Drug dealer caught with £1,000 cash rose through ranks to run Rochdale ‘Adam’ line - Asian Image
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A man who progressed from street dealing to managing other dealers in a Rochdale organised crime group has been jailed for 10 and a half years. Haider Ali, of Pike Street, Rochdale, played a significant role in the “Adam” drug line, which supplied crack cocaine and heroin across the area. Police began investigating Ali after receiving information about a suspected drug deal from a car parked in Baron Street, Rochdale town centre, shortly before midnight on 4 January 2025. Officers followed the vehicle until it stopped at a petrol station, where they blocked it from driving away. Ali, who was a passenger, got out and began walking quickly away before officers detained him. A search found more than £1,000 in cash and two mobile phones. After his arrest, further searches recovered two bundles containing wraps of brown and white substances which were later confirmed as heroin and cocaine. One of the prepaid phones seized from Ali was also identified as the device used to operate the Adam drug line.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Residents are being asked to donate new, unwrapped gifts for Rochdale borough’s Christmas Toy Appeal by Friday 11 December. The appeal supports local children living in poverty and distributed a record 10,000 toys to around 3,000 children last year. Number One Riverside Giving Back, a charity run by Rochdale Borough Council staff, is collecting gifts suitable for children aged up to 16. Donations can be left at local libraries and Your Trust leisure centres. Other collection points include the first-floor management office at Rochdale Riverside, The Trade Centre UK at Sandbrook Park and The Old Police Station in Heywood. Council volunteers will distribute the gifts in time for Christmas Day. Helen Walton, a council policy advisor from the Giving Back charity, said: “Christmas should be a magical time for every child, but for many families the financial pressures they face mean that even a small gift can feel impossible to afford. We’re already seeing requests for help, and that’s why every donation matters.” The appeal has been running since 2013 and is organised in partnership with Rochdale Borough Council, Rochdale Football Club and Your Trust. Organisers are encouraging donors to shop locally and choose sustainable gifts where possible.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale Borough Council’s staff-run charity ‘Number One Riverside Giving Back’ is now collecting donations for this year’s Christmas Toy Appeal, which helps make sure local children who are living in poverty have presents to open on December 25. The annual appeal, organised by council staff for the past thirteen years, is accepting donations at local libraries or Your Trust leisure centres until December 11. To help, all you need to do is donate an unwrapped, new gift suitable for a child up to 16 years-old and leave it at your local library or Your Trust leisure centre. There are also lots more collection points across the borough, including Rochdale Riverside retail and leisure destination (management office on first floor), The Trade Centre UK at Sandbrook Park, Rochdale and The Old Police Station in Heywood. You can find the full list of over 40 drop off points and other ways to donate at rochdale.gov.uk/ ChristmasToyAppeal Council volunteers, who distributed a record 10,000 toys last year to around 3,000 children will make sure they reach children in time for Christmas Day. Since 2013 the appeal has provided much needed festive cheer for thousands of children and teenagers. Council policy advisor Helen Walton, from the Giving Back charity said: “Christmas should be a magical time for every child, but for many families the financial pressures they face mean that even a small gift can feel impossible to afford. We’re already seeing requests for help, and that’s why every donation matters. Knowing there’s something to unwrap on Christmas morning will mean the world to a child. We’re incredibly grateful for the continued kindness of our communities, whose support helps bring joy and hope to families when they need it most.” Councillor Rachel Massey said: “No child should feel left out at Christmas, and this appeal helps ensure that thousands of children across our borough can experience the excitement and joy that every young person deserves. Behind every donated gift is a simple act of kindness that can have a lasting impact on a child and their family. I’m incredibly proud of the compassion shown by our communities every year, and I encourage anyone who can help to get involved.” As Christmas raises awareness of excess and waste, organisers are encouraging people to shop locally and, where possible, choose sustainable gifts – but above all, every donation, big or small, is really appreciated.

candidates.source_summary: A driver has been jailed for causing serious injury by dangerous driving following a pursuit through Rochdale in which a pedestrian was struck by a police car.
candidates.source_title: Driver jailed after Rochdale pursuit in which police car struck pedestrian
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A driver has been jailed for causing serious injury by dangerous driving following a pursuit through Rochdale in which a pedestrian was struck by a police car. Cameron Grainger, 25, was sentenced at Manchester Crown Court on Friday 6 November. The court heard Grainger had been drinking in Rochdale town centre before returning to his Seat Leon at around 3.25am on 19 November 2023. CCTV operators alerted police after seeing a man who appeared intoxicated preparing to drive away from Upper Broadfield Car Park. Grainger failed to stop for officers and drove at speed along Rochdale Road. CCTV showed him driving on the wrong side of the road. During the pursuit, a pedestrian, now aged 41, was struck by the police car. He suffered life-changing injuries. Officers stopped to give first aid, while Grainger continued driving before abandoning the Seat Leon on Wellington Street. CCTV showed him and three passengers running from the vehicle. Grainger was arrested the following day. Police also established that he was not insured to drive the car.

Every social landlord in England has to answer the same questions and the results are compared across all providers. candidates.source_body_excerpt: Licensees Cara and Martyn Benyon at the Dyers Arms in Littleborough, near Rochdale, have launched a new local pool league to bring players and pubs together, and are inviting more venues to enter their own teams. The Littleborough Pool League gives local players the opportunity to compete regularly, meet new people and enjoy friendly competition without having to travel miles. Created by Cara and Martyn, the league is also supported by pub regular Mark Jones, who helps with its organisation and administration. With seven pool teams already playing from the Dyers Arms, the licensees are now encouraging other pubs across Littleborough to get involved, including venues with a pool table that do not yet have a team. The pub is part of Admiral Taverns, the UK's leading community pub company with circa. 1,300 wet-led pubs across the UK. Cara and Martyn have run the Dyers Arms for the past three years, building a welcoming hub for local people to meet and socialise. Following a full refurbishment in 2025, which saw £180,000 spent on a complete redecoration, as well as the creation of a new beer garden they have continued to develop the pub’s sporting community, which includes darts and football teams alongside its pool players. Licensees Cara and Martyn Benyon commented : “Pool is a big part of what we do at the Dyers Arms, and we’re proud to have seven teams playing from the pub. We created the Littleborough Pool League to give local players more opportunities to compete within their own community, meet new people and support their local pubs. Martyn is a key player in the league himself, and they will also be launching a new ladies pool team which will start next season in March/April. “We’d love to hear from more pubs interested in entering a team, including those that have a pool table but haven’t set up a team yet." “We strongly believe in a local pub bringing together local people and the local community.”

candidates.source_title: CEAMS wins national award for sustainable manufacturing innovation
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The Centre of Expertise in Advanced Materials and Sustainability (CEAMS) and its project partners have been recognised nationally after winning the Sustainability and Circularity Award at the Composites UK Industry Awards. The award recognises pioneering work that could help transform how carbon fibre waste is reused across the aerospace sector and wider manufacturing industries. Working alongside Cygnet Texkimp, SHD Composites, NCC and Teledyne CML Composites, CEAMS successfully demonstrated a world-first aerospace component manufactured using prepreg material containing 100% recycled continuous carbon fibre. The project showed that recycled carbon fibre can achieve levels of stiffness and strength comparable to virgin material, while using existing industrial manufacturing processes. This creates a realistic route for large-scale adoption across advanced manufacturing sectors. The innovation also offers substantial environmental benefits. Previous CEAMS research estimated that recycled continuous carbon fibre may reduce carbon emissions by up to 80% when compared with virgin material, while helping create more resilient UK supply chains and higher-value uses for composite waste. As a founding partner of CEAMS, Rochdale Development Agency is proud to support innovation that brings together businesses, researchers and industry leaders to solve real-world challenges. This award is further evidence of Rochdale’s growing reputation as a centre for advanced manufacturing, materials innovation and sustainable industry, helping position the borough at the forefront of the technologies shaping the future economy. To find out more about the award and CEAMS’ award-winning work in sustainability and circularity, visit the Composites UK Industry Awards website or read the full winning case study.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale Borough Council’s staff-run charity 'Number One Riverside Giving Back' is now collecting donations for this year’s Christmas Toy Appeal. The appeal helps make sure local children who are living in poverty have presents to open on 25 December 2026. The annual appeal, organised by council staff for the past thirteen years, is accepting donations at local libraries or Your Trust leisure centres until Friday, 11 December 2026. Council policy advisor Helen Walton, from the Giving Back charity said: “Christmas should be a magical time for every child, but for many families the financial pressures they face mean that even a small gift can feel impossible to afford. We’re already seeing requests for help, and that’s why every donation matters. Knowing there’s something to unwrap on Christmas morning will mean the world to a child. We’re incredibly grateful for the continued kindness of our communities, whose support helps bring joy and hope to families when they need it most.” Parents, pupils and staff at Holy Trinity CE School in Littleborough collected gifts for the appeal last year, received by organiser Helen Walton. To help, all you need to do is donate an unwrapped, new gift suitable for a child up to 16 years-old and leave it at your local library or Your Trust leisure centre by Friday, 11 December 2026. There are also lots more collection points across the borough, including Rochdale Riverside retail and leisure destination (management office on first floor), The Trade Centre UK at Sandbrook Park, Rochdale and The Old Police Station in Heywood. Council volunteers, who distributed a record 10,000 toys last year to around 3,000 children will make sure they reach children in time for Christmas Day. Since 2013 the appeal has provided much needed festive cheer for thousands of children and teenagers.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: A man who played a significant role in an organised crime group which supplied class A drugs across Rochdale has been jailed for 10 years and six months. An investigation into Haider Ali was launched following information received that a drug deal had taken place from a car parked in Baron Street, in Rochdale town centre, just before midnight on January 4, 2025. Officers began to follow the vehicle and when it came to a stop at a local petrol station, officers immediately executed a reinforced stop to prevent it from making off. Ali, who was travelling as a passenger, exited the vehicle and began to speedily walk away before officers detained him. Following searches, Ali was found to be in possession of more than £1,000 in cash, and two mobile phones, all of which were seized. Ali was arrested on suspicion of being concerned in the supply of class A drugs and taken to custody where further searches recovered two bundles of several wraps of a brown and a white substance. Tests later confirmed these substances to be heroin and cocaine. A pre-paid mobile phone seized from Ali was confirmed to be the Adam drug line. Following this, investigators also uncovered that Ali was not only dealing drugs at street level, but he was also managing other street dealers. Evidence suggested that Ali had progressed from being a street dealer in 2014 to holding a significant role within the Adam OCG in 2024 into 2025, managing street dealers and the dedicated dealer phone, and directing those below him on where there next deal is.

Haider Ali, 34, was part of the ‘Adam’ line, which an organised crime gang operated to flood the town with cocaine and heroin. Police efforts to smash the drugs line were featured in the BBC series The Detectives: Taking Down An OCG, which shone a light on the gang based in the town. Minshull Street Crown Court heard previously that a CCTV operator spotted what appeared to be a drug deal in progress on Baron Street in Rochdale, and tipped off police. Officers followed a Nissan Qashqai car and when they swooped Ali ran away from the front passenger seat but was arrested a short distance away. On the dashboard in front of his seat police found 75 wraps of cocaine and 32 wraps of heroin. Ali was the 'controller' of the Adam drugs line, prosecutor Craig MacGregor said. Mobile phones seized by police were analysed. The 'Adam line' drug dealing operation, which was said to generate at least £1m-a-year. candidates.source_title: Rochdale residents stand together in silence to remember our nation's heroes - InYourArea
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Touching tributes and quiet reflection as crowds turn out to honour the fallen Parades and commemoration services brought crowds together to honour the nation's war heroes and pay their respects to those who made sacrifices in defence of the country. Representatives from the Navy, Army and Royal Air Force joined veterans and civic dignitaries for events in Rochdale town centre, Castleton, Heywood, Littleborough, Middleton, Norden, Milnrow and Wardle. Residents gathered as memorials fell silent, with the Last Post played at each service. Each ceremony included the immemorial words from Laurence Binyon’s 1914 poem, 'For the Fallen': "They shall grow not old as we that are left grow old; Age shall not weary them, nor the years condemn; at the going down of the sun and in the morning. We will remember them." The Armed Forces community, Members of Parliament, mayor of Rochdale, council leader, councillor Neil Emmott, councillors, faith leaders, local schools and members of the public also laid their own wreaths and gave respects, following moving readings of 'The Kohima Epitaph': "When you go home, tell them of us and say, for your tomorrow, we gave our today." Councillor Faisal Rana, mayor of Rochdale, said: "The turnout across the borough was incredible, as people of all ages gathered at memorials in Heywood, Middleton, Pennines, and Rochdale to pay their respects. On a poignant and moving Remembrance Day, we honoured the fallen, people of all faiths and no faith, from countries all over the world. It was a day when the whole community fell silent to reflect and remember. "We will forever hold a special place in our hearts, today and always, for those who never came home. Without their selfless dedication and sacrifices, the freedom, liberty and values we take for granted would have been lost. Side by side they fought together, they fell together and secured the peace together. We will always remember them. Lest we forget."

candidates.source_title: Rochdale completes £3.3m Warwick Mill purchase - Place North West
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Warwick Mill is a symbol of Middleton's decline, according to the co-chair of the town's MDC. Credit: via Rochdale Council The council has taken control of the derelict grade two-listed Middleton asset from Macau investor Kam Lei Fong and plans to refurbish it into hundreds of homes, a move the authority hopes will set the tone for the regeneration of the town. The former cotton mill, constructed in 1907, has been bought by Rochdale Council for £3.3m. The deal includes the 1960s London House next door, which will be demolished in the new year under Rochdale’s vision for the site. The council has yet to appoint a developer to refurbish the mill, one of Middleton’s best-loved assets. The deal, first revealed by Place North West in September, is the first major intervention since the creation of the Middleton Co-operative Mayoral Development Corporation. The MDC is led by actor and comedian Steve Coogan and chair of Co-operatives UK Rose Marley. It will oversee the town’s regeneration and is set to be formally established early next year. Cllr Neil Emmott, Leader of Rochdale Council, said: “Warwick Mill is a key historic asset in the heart of Middleton, and I know that local residents have long been frustrated that it’s fallen into such a state of disrepair and I share that frustration. We’ve wanted to see it brought back into use for a number of years, but we’ve seen no real progress under successive owners. “By buying it ourselves, we’re bringing it into public control and are now in a position to steer its future. Now it’s in our hands, we’re wasting no time in making immediate changes, with a local company leading this work for us.” He added: “As such a key part of this area’s history and a major building in the heart of Middleton, this is a huge regeneration opportunity, with new homes something we’re particularly keen to explore for this site. With the rapidly emerging Middleton MDC, the Warwick Mill project is just the first of a series of regeneration schemes which will change the face of this whole area.”

candidates.source_body_excerpt: The derelict building known as "Rochdale's Chernobyl" was once the world's largest producer of asbestos A derelict factory site in Greater Manchester that has been described as "Rochdale's Chernobyl" is being excavated in an attempt to locate buried asbestos. The old Turner Brothers factory in Spotland was once the world's largest producer of the toxic material. In recent years the site has been a magnet for disorder and trespass by so-called urban explorers. Owner Spodden Park Ltd will carry out investigations to locate where asbestos has been buried on the site, which has an area of about 75 acres (30 hectares). Asbestos is a heat and flame resistant material that is strong and cheap and has many uses. Microscopic fragments of all kinds of asbestos fibre are potentially dangerous when inhaled and may give rise to asbestos-related diseases including cancer. Spodden Park said asbestos would not be disturbed during the work.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Middleton’s regeneration has taken another major step forward with the council formally completing the purchase of Warwick Mill from developers, Kam Lei Fong. Once a thriving cotton mill, the imposing structure, which was built in 1907, has been vacant for at least a decade and has since become an eyesore, regularly attracting vandalism and urban explorers. The neighbouring 1960s office block, London House, has also been purchased as part of the £3.3 million deal, with plans to demolish the building. Work to transform the building will get under way quickly. Rochdale firm, Winterburns, is set to take over security immediately, with a beefed up, 24-hour presence on site. The firm will also start clearing the mountain of debris which has built up over years of neglect, including 1,000 tyres and overgrown plants and trees. Teams will soon start the delicate internal strip out of Warwick Mill and London House. The demolition of London House, a brutalist structure with little architectural merit, is set to get under way early in the New Year. The council will then kick start the process of tendering a developer partner to undertake the longer-term work of bringing Warwick Mill back into use. candidates.source_title: Education support service told it needs planning permission for hub - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A youth outreach hub and day-session centre which aims to stop children being excluded from school has been told it must apply for planning permission to continue operating at a business park in Rochdale. EdforAll Ltd applied to Rochdale Council for a Certificate of Lawfulness for its base at Unit 1, Crown Business Park, in Cowm Top Lane. Documents submitted with the application show it functions as an administrative headquarters for community outreach and a part-time, non-statutory support venue for local schools and young people aged 5 to 18. They add: “The proposed activities do not constitute a ‘school’ or standard educational facility. No change-of-use application is required as the operation aligns with Class E(f) (Day centre) and Class E(g)(i) (Offices). No internal structural changes or external building works are proposed.” It is described as an “intervention partner to local schools, providing short, part-time sessions to help students re-engage with their main education” and functions as a “part-time, non-statutory support venue for local schools and young people” and sessions held there are “intended to prevent school exclusion”, alongside basic literacy, numeracy, or functional skills training. A planning officer’s report said: “The case officer sought further clarification from the agent regarding the proposed use. The agent clarified that the facility would not be inspected by Ofsted, the Department for Education, or the CQC; and the facility would operate as alternative provision, with placements through referral of the local authority. “Based on the submitted details, further clarification, and the balance of probabilities, the proposed development would fail to meet the statutory definition of a day centre. candidates.source_title: Woman dies at Tesco after police called and store evacuated
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A woman tragically lost her life after emergency services were called to a Tesco supermarket. The incident took place at the store's branch on Silk Street, off Manchester Road on the outskirts of Rochdale, on Saturday afternoon (November 7). Greater Manchester Police (GMP) confirmed they received a call raising concerns for the welfare of a woman inside the shop. Eyewitnesses described how she was initially attended to by staff before paramedics took over upon their arrival. Shoppers reported being asked to vacate both the store and the car park to allow emergency services to manage the situation. It is believed that staff and management at the branch were on hand to assist throughout the unfolding incident. Video footage circulating on social media captured an air ambulance touching down in the supermarket's car park. Regrettably, despite the best efforts of those involved, the woman, who was in her 50s, could not be saved and passed away, a GMP spokesperson confirmed on Sunday afternoon, reports the Manchester Evening News . Her family have since been notified of her death. When contacted by the Manchester Evening News on Saturday, a Tesco spokesperson declined to offer any comment regarding the incident.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: A school has changed its name to better reflect the community it serves. Children at the Middleton primary school formed a giant star in their playground as they celebrated their school’s new name with a special visit from the Bishop of Middleton. Rhodes Green Church of England Primary School — previously known as Little Heaton CE Primary School — welcomed the Rt Revd Mark Davies on Thursday for a day of celebrations attended by pupils, staff, parents and members of the local community. The school, in Boardman Lane in Rhodes, officially changed its name in September as part of a fresh chapter under headteacher Chloe Noon. The new name reflects the school’s connection to the Rhodes community, where many of its children live and grow up, while its renewed identity is built around the Christian vision Shine as stars in the world. To mark the occasion, children gathered in the playground to form a giant star, captured in a photograph taken from above. Bishop Mark was also given a tour by the school’s head boy and head girl, visiting classrooms and meeting children from every year group before joining families for a special assembly. candidates.source_summary: From casualties and loss against the Ottomans, to success against the Germans on the Western Front, the Rochdale-based 6th Battalion, Lancashire Fusiliers bravely fought through the First World War, contributing directly to the victory of Britain and the Allies.
candidates.source_title: Lest We Forget as Rochdale battalion's valiant sacrifices during the First World War
candidates.source_body_excerpt: From casualties and loss against the Ottomans, to success against the Germans on the Western Front, the Rochdale-based 6th Battalion, Lancashire Fusiliers bravely fought through the First World War, contributing directly to the victory of Britain and the Allies. Britain declared war on Germany on 4th August 1914, after Germany breached the 1839 Treaty of London by invading Belgium, violating the neutrality of Belgium sworn by the 75 year old multilateral treaty signed by many nations, including the United Kingdom. Later this day, an order was sent to gather men to fight for the posterity of the nation, this was received in Rochdale in the afternoon of that same day that Belgium was invaded. The Rochdale Observer reported that 'a force of 900 men' answered the call to arms, and made way to the Baron Street drill hall. This was a grand shock, with huge crowds gathering, causing a crush that eventuated in the involvement of the police to hold back the crowd. The battalion stayed here until 20th August, when they left early in the morning for a training camp in Turton. The battalion was a unit of the Territorial Force, and was one of the first territorials to be taken overseas, setting sail for Egypt from Southampton on September 25th. They underwent training in Egypt, and joined with other battalions to become the 125th (Lancashire Fusiliers) Brigade in May 1915, before landing at Cape Helles in Gallipoli. Despite the failure of the Gallipoli campaign, the evacuation is remembered more fondly as an incredibly successful operation, and the remaining members of the 6th Battalion, Lancashire Fusiliers were withdrawn successfully. The 6th Battalion, Lancashire Fusiliers were then transferred to the Western Front, where they saw action at the Third Battle of Ypres, also known as the Battle of Passchendaele, and, in 1918, on the front lines in The Somme, the Battles of Hindenburg Line, and the Final Advance in Picardy, the last campaign being that which forced the surrender of Germany, ending World War 1. The sacrifices that were made all of the ~2000 Rochdale war dead are memorialised at the Cenotaph opposite the Town Hall, unveiled in 1922, where there will be a service to remember the sacrifices made by all people of Rochdale, especially the soldiers who fought for the posterity of this great nation. candidates.source_summary: From casualties and loss against the Ottomans, to success against the Germans on the Western Front, the Rochdale-based 6th Battalion, Lancashire Fusiliers bravely fought through the First World War, contributing directly to the victory of Britain and the Allies.
candidates.source_title: Lest We Forget: Rochdale battalion's valiant sacrifices during the First World War
candidates.source_body_excerpt: From casualties and loss against the Ottomans, to success against the Germans on the Western Front, the Rochdale-based 6th Battalion, Lancashire Fusiliers bravely fought through the First World War, contributing directly to the victory of Britain and the Allies. Britain declared war on Germany on 4th August 1914, after Germany breached the 1839 Treaty of London by invading Belgium, violating the neutrality of Belgium sworn by the 75 year old multilateral treaty signed by many nations, including the United Kingdom. Later this day, an order was sent to gather men to fight for the posterity of the nation, this was received in Rochdale in the afternoon of that same day that Belgium was invaded. The Rochdale Observer reported that 'a force of 900 men' answered the call to arms, and made way to the Baron Street drill hall. This was a grand shock, with huge crowds gathering, causing a crush that eventuated in the involvement of the police to hold back the crowd. The battalion stayed here until 20th August, when they left early in the morning for a training camp in Turton. The battalion was a unit of the Territorial Force, and was one of the first territorials to be taken overseas, setting sail for Egypt from Southampton on September 25th. They underwent training in Egypt, and joined with other battalions to become the 125th (Lancashire Fusiliers) Brigade in May 1915, before landing at Cape Helles in Gallipoli. The Gallipoli campaign is, unfortunately, remembered as being a failure, resulting in massive casualties and little gains. The 125th Brigade went into action firstly in the loss to the Ottomans at the Second Battle of Krithia, a three day battle that resulted in around a third of the 25,000 Allied soldiers that fought becoming casualties. They then fought at the Third Battle of Krithia and the Battle of Krithia Vineyard, both losses to the Ottomans, where casualties amongst three divisions at the latter battle, including that of the 125th Brigade, where the 6th Battalion, Lancashire Fusiliers were fighting, were 3,469. By August, around two thirds of the Rochdale 6th Battalion, Lancashire Fusiliers had been lost through battle casualties, injuries, sickness, etc. Despite the failure of the Gallipoli campaign, the evacuation is remembered more fondly as an incredibly successful operation, and the remaining members of the 6th Battalion, Lancashire Fusiliers were withdrawn successfully. The 6th Battalion, Lancashire Fusiliers were then transferred to the Western Front, where they saw action at the Third Battle of Ypres, also known as the Battle of Passchendaele, and, in 1918, on the front lines in The Somme, the Battles of Hindenburg Line, and the Final Advance in Picardy, the last campaign being that which forced the surrender of Germany, ending World War 1. Despite the battalion, and the brigade and division it was a part of, receiving immense loss and facing head-to-head with some of the worst battles for the Allies, the Rochdale-based battalion still came out of the war, thought numbers fewer, and were at the front lines during the Final Advance where the Germans eventually surrendered to the Allied forces.

candidates.source_summary: Baba Adeeko nets extra-time winner as Rochdale overcome Fleetwood in FA Cup Alloa Advertiser
candidates.source_title: Baba Adeeko nets extra-time winner as Rochdale overcome Fleetwood in FA Cup - Alloa Advertiser
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Substitute Baba Adeeko netted an extra-time winner as Rochdale progressed into the second round of the FA Cup by beating Fleetwood 2-1. Adeeko’s excellent first-time finish six minutes into the second period sent the vocal travelling support into ecstasy and sealed a second win at Highbury this campaign for Dale, following their success in the league back in late September. The hosts created the first clear opening of the game when striker Ronan Coughlan found space in the box but could only blaze a shot harmlessly over Sam Waller’s goal. Rochdale then took the lead after 23 minutes. Some slick one-touch football saw captain Harvey Gilmour combine with Charlie Tasker to set up Luke Hannant, who tapped in a neat first-time finish at the far post past Jay Lynch. Fleetwood pressed for an equaliser in the second half and went close when Harrison Neal’s effort from outside the box had to be gathered at the second attempt by Waller. The Cod Army levelled things up going into the last quarter of normal time thanks to a Coughlan penalty after Aaron Loupalo-Bi was hauled to the ground by Kaiden Wilson. Both teams went close in extra time before Adeeko’s winner, with Dale sub Bryant Bilongo failing to convert Tasker’s cross before Danny Andrew stung the palms of Waller with a well-struck free-kick.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: A man who led police on a high-speed town centre pursuit in which a patrol car hit and seriously injured a pedestrian has been jailed. Cameron Grainger, 25, was sentenced to four years and five months at Manchester Crown Court yesterday after he was found guilty of causing serious injury by dangerous driving. He has also been disqualified from diving for six years and two months. The court heard that at 1am on Sunday, November 19, 2023, Grainger parked his Seat Leon in the Upper Broadfield Car Park in Rochdale town centre, before spending almost three hours in bars and pubs in the area with three friends. CCTV footage showed Grainger consuming several alcoholic drinks before returning to his car at 3.25am. Concerned by his behaviour as he approached the car, CCTV operators alerted police that a man who appeared intoxicated was preparing to get behind the wheel and drive away. Officers were provided with a description of the vehicle, its registration number and the location it was leaving from. When officers attempted to stop the Seat Leon as it left the town centre, Grainger failed to stop and a short pursuit commenced.
